candidates: When adding a parser/grammar option that accepts a fixed set of string values, write parameterized unit tests using `it.each` that verify every valid value is accepted by the parser and reflected in the db getter.
New diagram syntax features must be covered by at least one Cypress snapshot test in `cypress/integration/rendering/` in addition to unit tests.

`ganttRenderer.js` duplicates tick-interval switch-case logic in two parallel blocks—one for `bottomXAxis` and one for `topXAxis`. Whenever either block is modified, apply the identical change to the other block to keep them in sync.

In Mermaid syntax documentation under `docs/syntax/`, code blocks that demonstrate diagram syntax should use the ` ```mermaid-example ` fence (not plain ` ```mermaid `) so the docs site renders both the source code and the resulting diagram.
New configuration properties and their default values must be defined in `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml` (using the `default:` key) rather than in `defaultConfig.ts`.

In `ganttDb.js`, module-level state variables must be initialised with an explicit default value at declaration (e.g., `let weekday = 'sunday'`) and reset to that same explicit value inside the `clear()` function; never leave them implicitly `undefined`.

When adding a keyword option with a fixed set of valid values to a `.jison` grammar file, define a separate lexer token for each valid value (e.g., `weekday\s+monday` → token `weekday_monday`) and corresponding grammar production rules that invoke the setter. Model this on the `direction` rule in `flow.jison`. Do not append a trailing `[^\n]*` wildcard to these token patterns.

In `config.schema.yaml` and `config.type.ts`, when a field accepts only a specific set of string literals, express the `tsType` (or TypeScript type) as a union of those literals alone—do not prepend `string |` to the union.
